newsitem.title: USA: Hillary Clinton to take active D.C. role - report.
newsitem.headline: Hillary Clinton to take active D.C. role - report.

text.p: First lady Hillary Clinton is trying to help solve the District of Columbia's financial and social problems and will express her interest in the city later this week, the Washington Post reported Wednesday.

Quoting unidentified administration sources, the newspaper said Hillary Clinton's decision to speak out about District affairs followed President Clinton's affirmation last week of commitment to the financially struggling city.
Mrs. Clinton is scheduled to speak Thursday at the unveiling of a $20 million program to provide loans for small businesses and housing in the District as well as a few other cities.
On Friday she will announce at Children's Hospital that she is donating a considerable part of the proceeds from her book "It Takes a Village" to the privately run hospital, the Post said.

President Clinton, who has been criticized in Washington for ignoring the plight of the nation's capital, acknowledged last week that his administration had not done enough to tackle its financial and social problems.
The Post said Hillary Clinton had waited until the president publicly affirmed the administration's interest in the District before deciding to make her own commitment public.
Mrs. Clinton's highly visible role in the president's failed first-term attempt to reform the nation's health-care system sparked bitter criticism, and she since has kept a lower political profile.

But the Post said Mrs. Clinton had been working behind the scenes on District issues, convening a meeting of major foundations Oct. 21 at the White House to round up support for programs started by a group of local churches.
